acceptance.given: When the applicable Consumer enable operation is exercised through the Toolchain replay path, the invocation is routed to the real Consumer call surface and reaches the production implementation.

oracle.expected: The selected Consumer's real call surface records or exposes a successful enable execution, and the resulting evidence identifies the concrete Consumer invocation rather than a simulation, stub, or non-real path.
forbidden: Enable is executed only through a simulated, mocked, stubbed, or otherwise non-real call surface.
oracle.observable: A targeted replay test invokes the Consumer through its real call surface and asserts the recorded successful enable event and its concrete call-surface identity.

acceptance.then: The assertion passes only when the real Consumer call surface has executed enable successfully.
acceptance.when: After exercising enable for each applicable Consumer in the replay test.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Target the real Consumer enable invocation and fail when no successful enable execution is recorded.
Target the call-surface identity assertion and fail when enable is routed through a simulation, mock, stub, or other non-real path.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make the replay path exercise enable through the real applicable Consumer call surface and expose a concrete successful execution record for that invocation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing replay interfaces and evidence formats; rollback only the Consumer enable routing/evidence assertion change.

slice_hint.state_transition: Applicable Consumer requires enable execution -> real Consumer call surface executes enable successfully and records/exposes that execution.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every applicable Consumer exercised by the test has a successful enable record whose call-surface identity is the real production Consumer surface; absence or simulation causes failure.
